title: AHC Capability
description: One harness capability. The normative unit of the AI Harness Catalog. A capability states WHAT MUST EXIST in a system, tags WHICH archetypes need it, names WHERE it can physically live, and records the design decisions its builder must make. A capability never states a verification obligation (that is the assurance catalog's job), never names a product, and never sets a threshold.

id.description: Flat, permanent, never reused. Layer and archetype are metadata, not identity — see docs/ID-POLICY.md.

status.description: Deprecated and superseded capabilities stay in the catalog forever so citations keep resolving.

since.description: Catalog version in which this capability first appeared.

level.description: Strength, RFC 2119 usage, binding only within an adopting organisation.

layers.description: Which part of the harness owns this. Tags, not a tree. More than two usually means the capability is really two capabilities.

positions.description: Where this can physically live. Order is meaningful: the first is the primary position, the rest are backstops or alternatives.

concern.description: Which kind of quality this capability exists to serve — one of the ten in taxonomy/concerns.yaml (ISO/IEC 25010:2023, plus cost). Exactly one, chosen by what the capability's own failure_mode says goes wrong FIRST when it does not exist. Drives the Concern View, which joins on this string across all six specs in the family.

facet.description: Optional. A 25010:2023 sub-characteristic of the concern, where the characteristic alone is too coarse to be useful. The linter checks it belongs to the concern named.

archetypes.description: Tags, not a tree. Core capabilities enumerate every archetype explicitly so a consumer never has to resolve inheritance. Vocabulary is pinned from the assurance catalog.

core.description: True if every AI application needs this regardless of shape. Presentational: core capabilities already list all archetypes.

requirement.description: What must exist, in plain English. States the component and the constraint on it. Contains no verification language, no product names, no thresholds.

failure_mode.description: What actually goes wrong in a system that lacks this. Concrete and specific — this is the field that justifies the capability's existence, and a vague one is a sign the capability is a principle rather than a component.

discharges.description: Assurance catalog obligations this capability makes verifiable. The join between the two catalogs. An obligation cannot be discharged by a component that does not exist.

design_decisions.description: The choices a builder must make. This is the substance of the catalog — a capability with no decisions is either trivial or under-specified.

key.description: Stable slug for this decision within its capability, forming the identifier AHC-####/key that a profile answers. Permanent and never reused, on the same argument as the capability identifier itself: a rename breaks every profile that recorded an answer. Optional while the catalog is being keyed; a decision without one cannot be answered in a machine-readable way.

tension.description: What is genuinely traded away by each answer. If nothing is traded away, it is not a decision.

resolution.description: A defensible default, where one exists. Omit rather than invent one — a decision with no general answer is the most useful kind to surface.

realization_policy.description: 'own' — the construction question is genuinely different from the verification question, so realizations/ may carry build options for this capability. 'see_aac' — the assurance catalog already enumerates the same machinery, so realizations/ must carry none and the reader is pointed there instead. This is the anti-duplication rule; the linter enforces it.

realization_note.description: Required when realization_policy is 'see_aac'. States what this catalog adds beyond the assurance catalog's realization options — usually a positional or structural constraint — and nothing more.

see_also.description: Related capabilities. Not inheritance and not a dependency graph.
